title: FDA rejects ITM Isotope’s radiopharma therapy over manufacturing issues
snippet: ITM Isotope Technologies plans on resubmitting its advanced cancer radiopharma therapy to the FDA after addressing the agency’s concerns.

title: Scholar Rock rejigs approval filing after FDA flags violations at Novo plant
snippet: Despite earlier claims of improvement at the fill-finish plant, the FDA has classified the facility as Official Action Indicated based on inspection findings.

title: After billions in deals, Insilico CEO promises: ‘You haven't seen anything yet’
snippet: Insilico Medicine CEO Alex Zhavoronkov’s mad dash across the BIO International Convention in June attracted plenty of eyes. But the executive would prefer industry watchers gawk at the billions of dollars’ worth of deals his company has struck.

title: Epicrispr, Infinimmune snag combined $165M in VC cash
snippet: Epicrispr Biotechnologies is working on an epigenetic medicine for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, while Infinimmune will advance a pair of antibodies for atopic dermatitis.

title: AbCellera’s menopause medicine ‘sets new efficacy bar’ for hot flashes
snippet: AbCellera Biologics’ reduction in hot flashes sets it apart from currently commercial oral drugs, including Astellas’ Veozah and Bayer’s Lynkuet, according to BMO Capital Markets.

title: Silence causes uproar in rare blood cancer space as data sets high bar for competitors
snippet: The mid-stage win of Silence Therapeutics’ siRNA drug in polycythemia vera validates the therapeutic approach of similar assets in development—but also sets a high standard for therapies from Takeda, Agios and Disc Medicine.

title: Vaderis fuels up with $152M series B to test rare vascular disease in Phase 3
snippet: Vaderis is hoping that engasertib will become the first approved medicine for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, a rare condition that can cause spontaneous bleeding.

title: Austria’s new growth fund could further bolster its dynamic biotech innovation economy
snippet: The national growth vehicle isn’t biotech‑dedicated, but channeling capital toward life sciences would amplify Austria’s strong research hubs, nondilutive funding landscape and reputation as a champion in science and technology.

title: BMS picks Texas for new $2.3B manufacturing campus
snippet: Bristol Myers Squibb’s $2.3 billion Houston manufacturing campus is part of the company’s larger $40 billion investment designed to bolster American innovation and manufacturing.

title: Sionna’s cystic fibrosis failure is a windfall for Vertex’s blockbuster franchise
snippet: A surprise flop in Phase 2a cystic fibrosis trial sent Sionna’s shares plummeting, but for Vertex, the news reinforced its standard-of-care standing with highly successful drugs like Trikafta.

title: aTyr will cut 60% of workforce, Arpeggio shutters
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Jazz commits up to $1.3B to buy Actio, bolster epilepsy pipeline
snippet: Jazz Pharmaceuticals is reaching into its wallet once again, this time buying Actio Biosciences and an experimental therapy for KCNT1+ epilepsy, a form of the disease with no FDA-approved treatments.

title: All eyes on psychedelic drugmakers as Definium, Compass near major catalysts
snippet: Definium Therapeutics’ closely watched anxiety readout could further validate its single-dose LSD candidate, while Compass Pathways advances a psilocybin program through a rolling FDA filing.

title: AstraZeneca partners with CSPC to build Chinese biologics manufacturing plant
snippet: News of the joint venture comes months after AstraZeneca vowed to spend $15 billion in China by the end of the decade.

title: Tenax shares nosedive as heart failure drug fails in Phase 3
snippet: Patients treated with Tenax Therapeutics’ heart failure drug TNX-103 did not show significantly better functional performance—though Leerink analysts found biomarker improvements and subgroup analyses in elderly and more severe patients “very encouraging.”

title: BlossomHill, Latigo bloom on Nasdaq with oversubscribed IPOs
snippet: BlossomHill Therapeutics will use its $150 million IPO proceeds to power the Phase 1/2 development of a non-small cell lung cancer drug, while Latigo Therapeutics will bring in more than $345 million for its late-stage non-opioid pain pill.

title: BioMarin axes asset from $270M Inozyme takeover, ending run in rare metabolic indication
snippet: BioMarin’s discontinued drug showed biomarker benefits in a Phase 3 study for ENPP1 deficiency but these failed to translate to clinical improvements.

title: Denali climbs past Avlayah expectations with $3.6M in revenue
snippet: After launching in April, Hunter syndrome drug Avlayah surprised analysts with a strong first quarter, as patients rush to get access to Denali Therapeutics’ new option.

title: From ex vivo to in vivo: Shaping the next generation of viral vector manufacturing
snippet: The shift from ex vivo to in vivo gene delivery is rewriting the rules of viral vector manufacturing, forcing developers to rethink scale, purity, cell lines and analytics as vectors themselves become the drug. AGC Biologics is betting on stable producer lines, next‑gen purification and deeper characterization to meet...

title: Biogen’s targeted ALS treatment is reversing decline in some patients. Can more be helped?
snippet: Three years after Qalsody was approved by the FDA as the first drug to target a genetic cause of ALS, some patients are reporting not only disease stabilization but also improvement of symptoms.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
